title: Finite sums cancel under a fixed-point-free involution
statement: Let $T$ be a set, $E\subseteq T$ a finite subset [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set], and $G$ an additive commutative monoid (a set with associative commutative addition and a zero element). Let $f:T\to G$ and let $\tau:E\to E$ satisfy $\tau(\tau(x))=x$ and $\tau(x)\ne x$ for every $x\in E$. Suppose $f(x)+f(\tau(x))=0$ for every $x\in E$. Then $$\sum_{x\in E}f(x)=0.$$ The finite subset $E$ may be empty.
